dct_description_sm: Monitoring and responding to climate change impacts on water resources is emerging as a national and territorial priority. Climate change has already and will continue to alter the hydrological cycle in the north (i.e., changes in volume and timing of river flows). In order to determine the impacts of climate change on water resources and adapt to these changes, water resource managers, academics and the public need access to water data and information.   This multi-year project was developed to ensure that the products of government water programs in Yukon meet the needs of water users as the impacts of climate change become apparent. The main objectives of this project were: (1) to increase the accessibility and availability of water data and information through creation of a web-based information tool; and (2) to provide an assessment of climate change vulnerabilities in the Yukon.   The project identified adaptive management actions for water users to respond to changes, as well as determined that the water programs are focussed on meeting users' needs. Also, knowledge of water and impacts of climate change on water quality and supply were improved to benefit decision-makers. The main objective of the second year of this project was to create a Water Information Tool beta which includes information and data concerning Yukon's hydrologic and water management regimes. The original database was maintained by ensuring source data consistency. Documentation of existing and forecasted uses of Yukon's water was completed. A water quantity and quality data collection adaptation plan was developed for water managers. Finally, the final Risk and Vulnerability Assessment of Yukon Water Resources was drafted.

dct_title_s: Adaptive Management for Water Users Responding to Climate Change
